stemMd: A manager argues: “Every project that met our quality target had a peer review. This project had a peer review, so it must have met the target.” The reasoning is flawed because it

options.label: A
options.textMd: treats a necessary condition in the evidence as though it were sufficient.

options.label: B
options.textMd: assumes that no project can have two reviewers.

options.label: C
options.textMd: infers a population trend from a numerical average.

options.label: D
options.textMd: confuses an increase in percentage with an increase in total.

options.label: E
options.textMd: denies that any successful project was reviewed.

explanationMd: The premise gives success implies review. Review can also occur in unsuccessful projects, so reversing the implication is unjustified.
